CAQM invokes Stage-I of GRAP in Delhi-NCR with immediate effect amid sharp rise in AQI
articles.full_content:
Delhi recorded a daily average Air Quality Index (AQI) of 244 (‘Poor’ category) at 2 PM today, as per the daily AQI Bulletin provided by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB). Further, daily average AQI rose to 245 (‘Poor’ category) at 4PM.
In view of the average/ overall air quality of Delhi recording ‘Poor’ category (AQI ranging between 201-300), the CAQM Sub-Committee on GRAP met today to take stock of the current air quality scenario of Delhi-NCR. While comprehensively reviewing the air quality scenario in the region as well as forecast for weather/ meteorological conditions by IMD/ IITM and air quality index of Delhi, the Sub-Committee decided to invoke all 25 action points as per Stage-I of the extant GRAP with immediate effect, in the entire NCR.
Actions under Stage-I of the extant GRAP would be implemented, monitored and reviewed by all the agencies concerned in the entire NCR to ensure that the AQI levels do not slip further. All implementing agencies would keep strict vigil and intensify measures of the extant GRAP schedule.
Following are the 25 action points as per Stage-I of the extant GRAP:
Stage I – ‘Poor’ Air Quality
(DELHI AQI ranging between 201-300)
• Ensure proper implementation of Directions/ Rules/ Guidelines for enforcement of dust mitigation measures (C&D materials & waste are properly stored & duly covered, transportation of C&D materials/ waste only in covered vehicles, yardsticks for anti-smog guns, water sprinkling etc.) in Construction and Demolition (C&D) activities and sound environmental management of C&D waste.
• Ensure strict compliance of Direction Nos. 11-18 dated 11.06.2021 and do not permit C&D activities in respect of such C&D projects with plot size equal to or more than 500 sqm, which are not registered on the ‘web portal’ of the respective State / GNCTD and / or which do not fulfil the other requirements as per the above noted statutory Directions, for remote monitoring of dust mitigation measures.
• Ensure regular lifting of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW), C&D waste, Industrial and Hazardous waste from dedicated dump sites/ industrial areas and ensure that no waste is dumped illegally in open land areas.
• Carry out periodic mechanized sweeping and water sprinkling on roads and ensure scientific disposal of the dust collected in designated sites/landfills.
• Intensify use of anti-smog guns, water sprinkling and dust suppression measures in road construction / widening / repair projects and maintenance activities.
• Strictly enforce prohibition on open burning of bio-mass and municipal solid waste. Impose maximum EC upon violations in accordance with Hon’ble NGT’s orders dated 04.12.2014 and 28.04.2015 in OA 21/2014.
• Intensify vigil to ensure that there are no burning incidents in the landfill sites / dumpsites.
• Synchronize traffic movements and deploy adequate personnel at all identified corridors with heavy traffic, congestion points/ intersections for smooth flow of traffic.

DoPT Launches Special Campaign 6 with Swachhata Pledge, Cleanliness Drive and Tree Plantation on Swachh Bharat Diwas; Focus on Swachhata, Disposal of Pendencies, Records Management and E-Waste
articles.full_content:
The Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) has successfully completed the Preparatory Phase of Special Campaign 6 and formally launched the Implementation Phase on 2 nd October, 2026, coinciding with Swachh Bharat Diwas. The Implementation Phase will continue till 31 st October, 2026. The Campaign, being undertaken by the Government with the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances (DARPG) as the nodal Department, seeks to strengthen Swachhata, improve efficiency, promote digital governance, improve work environment and culture, ensure timely disposal of pending matters and promote better management of official resources.
The launch event was held at Grih Kalyan Kendra, Lodhi Road, New Delhi, with Secretary (P) as the Chief Guest. The programme included the Swachhata Oath, a cleanliness drive, floral tributes to Mahatma Gandhi, tree plantation and cultural presentations on the theme of cleanliness, and concluded with the felicitation of Swachhata Karmayogis.
During the Preparatory Phase, which was carried out from 16 th to 30 th September 2026, DoPT undertook a detailed assessment of VIP references, Public Grievances, Parliamentary Assurances and other matters requiring time-bound action. The exercise enabled the Department to identify priority areas and formulate targeted interventions for their expeditious disposal during the Implementation Phase.
The exercise was undertaken across DoPT and its Attached and Subordinate Offices. Along with the above, DoPT and its offices have finalised action plans covering cleanliness drives, disposal of pending matters, records management and freeing up of office space across various locations for focused cleanliness and space-management activities, with emphasis on creating cleaner, more organised and productive workspaces.
A comprehensive review of physical and electronic records, office scrap and other materials requiring weeding out/disposal was also carried out. The Department and its associated offices identified records for digitisation, obsolete documents for weeding out and opportunities for better utilisation of available office space. These measures are expected to contribute to improved workplace efficiency and more effective management of institutional resources.
As part of the Preparatory Phase, the Department has uploaded the requisite targets for Special Campaign 6 on the SCDPM 6 portal of DARPG, which will be used to monitor and review the progress of the campaign.
In line with this year’s emphasis of the Campaign on effective collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste, DoPT has kept a special focus on this component as well. Stakeholders across the Department and its associated offices have been sensitised to ensure that e-waste is appropriately identified, segregated, disposed of and managed in accordance with the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022, with progress to be tracked on the Special Campaign 6 Portal being updated by DARPG.

DGFT Chennai Flags Off First Gem and Jewellery Consignment to New Zealand Under New FTA
articles.full_content:
The office of the Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Chennai, flagged off a major consignment of gems and jewellery to New Zealand, ahead of the India–New Zealand Free Trade Agreement (FTA) coming into force on October 20, 2026.
Smt. Rajalakshmi Devaraj, Additional DGFT, formally flagged off the inaugural shipment, valued at Rs. 63,78,753, manufactured by M/s. Emerald Jewel Industry India Limited. Representatives from the Gem and Jewellery Export Promotion Council (GJEPC) and key industry stakeholders participated in the event.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Diaan Sakthi Sreenivasan, Whole-time Director, Business Development, Emerald Jewel Industry India Limited, highlighted the enhanced trade opportunities and competitive edge the new tariff preferences under the FTA will provide to the domestic gem and jewellery sector in expanded international markets.

CSIR-NIScPR Successfully Concludes Two-Week Skill Training Programme on Library Automation, Digitisation and Artificial Intelligence for Libraries
articles.full_content:
The CSIR-National Institute of Science Communication and Policy Research (CSIR-NIScPR) successfully organised a two-week skill training programme on “Skill Training in Library Automation, Digitization and Artificial Intelligence for Libraries” during 5–16 October 2026 under the CSIR Integrated Skill Initiative (Phase III). Organised by the Institute’s Training Division, the programme aimed to strengthen the technical competencies of library and information science professionals, academicians, researchers, students and IT professionals in library automation, digitisation, digital repository management and the application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in library services. A total of 16 participants from universities, research institutions, libraries, and other organizations across the country attended the programme.
Dr. Geeta Vani Rasayam, Director, CSIR-NIScPR, inaugurated the programme and encouraged participants to actively engage in the training. Shri Mukesh A. Pund, Head, Training Division, CSIR-NIScPR, introduced the objectives of the programme and highlighted the importance of skill development in library automation, digitisation and the adoption of emerging technologies. Shri Salim Ansari moderated the inaugural session.
Designed with an emphasis on experiential learning, the programme combined expert lectures, demonstrations and hands-on sessions on Koha Integrated Library Management System (ILMS) and DSpace digital repository software.
The Koha sessions covered open-source software fundamentals, installation of the Linux operating system and Koha, catalogue management, patron management, circulation workflows, report generation, system customisation, and backup and restoration. Participants gained practical experience in configuring and managing library automation functions and workflows.
The DSpace sessions focused on installation and administration, management of communities and collections, item submission, e-people registration and authorisation, Dublin Core and Bitstream Registry management, basic customisation, and backup and restoration. These sessions provided practical exposure to digital repository management for the organisation, preservation and dissemination of scholarly and institutional knowledge.
The programme also covered emerging applications of Artificial Intelligence in libraries, including AI tools and metadata extraction using AI. A special session on iThenticate was conducted on 15 October 2026 to familiarise participants with text similarity checking and its relevance to responsible academic and scholarly writing.
As part of the programme, participants visited the National Science Library to gain insights into its resources and services. The academic sessions were conducted by Shri Mukesh Pund, Shri Sanjay Burde, Dr. Avinash Kshitij, Shri Salim Ansari and Shri Bharath Natarajan. The practical exercises enabled participants to apply the concepts covered during the training.
